requirement: A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.ci.fence_lengths`. I did not request implementation source.

**1. Opening fences of at least three colons are accepted (MAY four or more, MUST accept any length from three).**
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers]` runs openers of 4 and 7 colons through `validate_repository`. It asserts one requirement is found and no errors are reported. The recorded body must match the extracted body exactly, so a wrong span would produce an error.
- The three-colon opener is covered by `fn[colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text]` and by `fn[example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace]`, which uses a `:::{req}` fence.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive]` and `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code]` cover 4-colon openers at the parser level.

**2. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener stays inside the body.**
- `fn[a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive]` has a `::::` opener with a nested `:::{note}` and a bare `:::` line. It asserts the exact body, `"Intro.\n\n:::{note}\nNested.\n:::\n"`, and that "Outside." falls after the end.
- The evidence test repeats this for 4-, 5- and 7-colon openers. The nested `:::` stays in the body, and the text after the nested block, "Still in the requirement.", is still part of it.
- `fn[markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code]` asserts the outer `a.b` body includes the nested `:::{impl}` block and its bare `:::`. It also asserts the inner `c.d` fence is parsed separately.

**3. A closing fence with at least as many colons as the opener ends the body.**
- Equal length is tested with `::::`/`::::`.
- Longer closers are tested with 4/5 and 7/8 colons. The `src/fenced.rs` test also has `:::` closed by an indented `   :::::  `.
- Text after the closer is excluded. The evidence tests check this through validation, and the `src/lib.rs` test asserts it directly.
- `fn[example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace]` covers `{example}` blocks with 4/5 and 6/7 colon fences and asserts the extracted text.

**4. "Outside a fenced code example": colon lines inside code fences do not close the body.**
- `fn[colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text]` puts a bare `:::` inside a ```text block in a `:::` requirement. The body must include it, and the requirement after it must still be found.
- The `src/fenced.rs` test has a code fence containing `:::{cite} e.f`, and it is skipped when code fences are honored. The plain-text mode count of 4 contrasts with the markdown-mode count of 3.
- The example test has a code fence containing `:::{example} literal`. It asserts that `rules.literal` is not defined.

Each test carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. I found no obligation without an exercising test and an assertion on its outcome, and no marking gap.
